Information criteria for a graph-structured fit

Source: R/criteria.R
mc_compute_criterion.Rd

Computes working AIC and BIC, the quasi-likelihood information criterion (QIC), a Godambe-adjusted working BIC (GBIC) and the extended BIC (EBIC), all built on the Gaussian working log-criterion \(\ell^p_e\) of mc_graph_ploglik. With \(p\) the number of free parameters of the between-response covariance (diagonal and edge parameters) and \(n\) the number of units (rows of the residual matrix), $$\mathrm{AIC} = -2\ell^p_e + 2p,\qquad \mathrm{BIC} = -2\ell^p_e + \log(n)\,p,$$ $$\mathrm{QIC} = -2\ell^p_e + 2\,d_{\mathrm{eff}},\qquad \mathrm{GBIC} = -2\ell^p_e + \log(n)\,d_{\mathrm{eff}},$$ with the effective dimension \(d_{\mathrm{eff}}=\mathrm{tr}(H^{-1}V)\). Here \(H\) is the curvature (sensitivity) and \(V\) the empirical variability of the Pearson estimating functions, both per unit, so that the trace is invariant to the scale. Under the Gaussian working model, when \(H = V = J\), the effective dimension reduces to the parameter count and QIC and GBIC reduce to AIC and BIC. "clbic" is an exact alias of "gbic"; it does not assert a composite-likelihood factorization. Smaller values indicate a better working model.

Usage

mc_compute_criterion(
  fit,
  which = c("aic", "bic", "qic", "gbic", "clbic", "ebic"),
  ebic_gamma = 0.5,
  cluster = NULL,
  small_sample = FALSE
)

Arguments

fit

an object of class "mcglm_graph".

which

character vector among "aic", "bic", "qic", "gbic", "clbic" and "ebic". "clbic" is an alias of "gbic". When left out, the first five are returned; "ebic" is computed only when requested.

ebic_gamma

the parameter \(\gamma\ge0\) of the extended BIC (default 0.5), used only when "ebic" is requested.

cluster

optional independent-cluster identifier, one per residual row (at least two distinct values, no missing values). For QIC and GBIC, Pearson contributions are summed within clusters before forming their empirical variability. BIC, GBIC and EBIC use the logarithm of the number of independent clusters, instead of the number of rows, in their penalty. Supplying the identifier does not by itself establish independence of the clusters or centering of their scores.

small_sample

logical; multiply the clustered variability by \(G/(G-1)\), with \(G\) the number of clusters; ignored without cluster.

Value

A named numeric vector of the requested criteria, carrying the attributes "criterion_status" ("godambe", "godambe_pseudoinverse", "parameter_count_fallback" or "not_required") and "effective_dimension" (the value of \(d_{\mathrm{eff}}\), NA when no Godambe-adjusted criterion was requested). A status other than "godambe" means the effective dimension could not be computed from a well-conditioned sensitivity (a spectral pseudo-inverse or, last, the parameter count was used instead) and must be reported as such.

Details

With cluster, the logarithmic multiplier \(\log(n)\) of BIC, GBIC and EBIC becomes \(\log(G)\), with \(G\) the number of independent clusters, and the variability \(V\) is formed from the contributions summed within clusters. The criterion \(\ell^p_e\), which remains a sum over the \(n\) rows, the parameter count \(p\), AIC and the multiplier 2 of QIC are not altered.

The extended BIC

"ebic" is the form of Foygel and Drton (2010) for Gaussian graphical models, \(\mathrm{EBIC}_\gamma=\mathrm{BIC}+4\gamma|E|\log R\), with \(|E|\) the number of edge parameters of the fit and \(R\) the number of responses. The diagonal parameters are common to every candidate support, so they enter through the BIC alone and do not alter differences between supports. \(\gamma=0\) gives the BIC back. It is offered as a working criterion: its consistency for the graph is established for Gaussian likelihoods, and it does not carry over, as such, to the working criterion of the residual layer.

Scope of the Godambe penalties

For a sparse DAG, \(H\) is the observed curvature of the residual working criterion. It can differ from the model-based Pearson sensitivity when the fitted covariance is misspecified. For the linear-precision GGM they agree. The QIC optimism calculation assumes genuinely known first-stage marginal parameters. With marginals estimated on the same data, QIC remains a working criterion; the reported penalty is not an exact two-stage optimism correction. The empirical variability is \(V=n^{-1}\sum_i\psi_i\psi_i^\top\), with \(\psi_i\) the Pearson contribution of unit \(i\) (summed within clusters when cluster is given, then divided by \(n\)). It estimates the variance of the scores only when their means vanish per independent unit or cluster (or the aggregate contribution of squared means vanishes). A pooled zero score is insufficient.

References

Foygel, R. and Drton, M. (2010). Extended Bayesian information criteria for Gaussian graphical models. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 23, 604–612.

Pan, W. (2001). Akaike's information criterion in generalized estimating equations. Biometrics 57(1), 120–125. doi:10.1111/j.0006-341X.2001.00120.x

Gao, X. and Song, P. X.-K. (2010). Composite likelihood Bayesian information criteria for model selection in high-dimensional data. Journal of the American Statistical Association 105(492), 1531–1540. doi:10.1198/jasa.2010.tm09414

Varin, C. and Vidoni, P. (2005). A note on composite likelihood inference and model selection. Biometrika 92(3), 519–528. doi:10.1093/biomet/92.3.519

See also

mc_graph_ploglik, mc_graph_stepwise, mc_select_lambda, mc_graph_cv.

Other information criteria: mc_graph_cv(), mc_graph_ploglik()

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1); n <- 150; x <- rnorm(n)
d <- data.frame(y1 = rnorm(n), y2 = rnorm(n), y3 = rnorm(n), x = x)
f <- mcglm_graph(list(y1~x, y2~x, y3~x), data = d)
#> Automatic initial values selected.
mc_compute_criterion(f, c("aic", "bic", "qic", "gbic"))
#>      aic      bic      qic     gbic 
#> 1282.718 1300.782 1283.775 1303.430 
#> attr(,"criterion_status")
#> [1] "godambe"
#> attr(,"effective_dimension")
#> [1] 6.528506
mc_compute_criterion(f, "ebic", ebic_gamma = 0.5)
#>     ebic 
#> 1307.374 
#> attr(,"criterion_status")
#> [1] "not_required"
#> attr(,"effective_dimension")
#> [1] NA
# }
